vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: scihub-paper-downloader
Version: 1.0.3

The skill is a legitimate tool for resolving DOIs to PDF links via Sci-Hub mirrors. The bundled Python script (scihub-paper-downloader.py) uses the standard library to fetch pages, handle cookies, and implement a Proof-of-Work solver for Altcha CAPTCHAs. It includes robust DOI normalization and PDF verification logic. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or prompt injection was found; the code is well-structured and aligns strictly with its stated purpose.

llm.summary: This skill does what it says at a high level, but it uses Sci-Hub automation with under-disclosed anti-bot solving and unsafe untrusted URL probing that warrants Review before installation.

dimensions.detail: Network access is proportionate to DOI resolution, but the implementation accepts mirror-provided candidate URLs and follows redirects without scheme, host, or private-network restrictions, creating an overbroad network-request surface for the stated task.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains a short SKILL.md and one bundled Python script using only the Python standard library; no package installation, remote code retrieval, shell execution, or dependency setup was found.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md discloses Sci-Hub lookup and OA fallback behavior, but it does not warn that DOIs are sent to Sci-Hub mirrors, candidate URLs are fetched, custom mirrors can be supplied through SCIHUB_MIRRORS, or CAPTCHA-like challenges may be solved automatically.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No persistence, credential storage, privilege escalation, scheduled tasks, memory writes, local profile access, or durable background behavior was found; cookies are kept only in an in-memory cookie jar during execution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is Sci-Hub DOI-to-PDF resolution, and the bundled script aligns with that overall goal, but it also automatically solves Sci-Hub ALTCHA challenges and probes PDF URLs scraped from third-party HTML without clear disclosure or destination validation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with an agent contacting Sci-Hub mirrors and third-party PDF hosts using your DOI queries. Run it in a network-restricted sandbox that blocks localhost, private networks, link-local addresses, and metadata services, and avoid using custom SCIHUB_MIRRORS unless you fully trust them. Be aware that Sci-Hub access may be legally or institutionally restricted and that the script automates challenge solving.
llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Using a bundled networked Python resolver is expected for this skill, but the artifact does not define least-privilege tool or network boundaries.
[SQP-2] expected: Sci-Hub use is central to the skill, but the skill lacks prominent legal, compliance, privacy, and source-trust warnings.
[SDI-4] expected: The script docstring is narrower than runtime behavior, but SKILL.md explicitly documents the OA_LINK fallback, so this is documentation inconsistency rather than hidden behavior.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The code contains explicit ALTCHA challenge solving and submission logic, which is not clearly disclosed in the skill instructions and creates service-abuse and compliance risk.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending the DOI to Sci-Hub mirrors and checking discovered PDF candidates fits the resolver purpose, but it is under-disclosed and exposes user research metadata to third-party services.
[SDI-1] expected: OA fallback extraction is disclosed in SKILL.md, so this finding is downgraded as purpose-aligned and documented.
[SQP-3] expected: The hard-coded Accept-Language header is minor and not material to the verdict.
[T09] unexpected: The SSRF-style concern is supported by artifact evidence: mirror HTML is used to generate candidate URLs, those URLs are fetched with automatic redirects, and there is no public-host or private-network blocking.
